clue.text: Put off, seeing pop style madness surrounding 'Posh'

indicators.note: the two words before it are read as one string that goes around the word for posh

parts.note: disco is a style of pop music
rage can mean madness or fury
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone is put off by a dance-floor craze that has gone wild around a fashionable celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' in quotes suggests a nickname, but it is just the old label for upper-class usage; 'surrounding' has the two outer words wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to deter them, synonymous with putting them off.

clue.text: Destroy tree that has died first

indicators.note: the letter for died is placed at the front, ahead of the tree

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree that died earlier is to be cut down and destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to destroy or wreck them, a synonym.

clue.text: Singles out for empty love in groups

indicators.note: the emptied word goes inside the word for groups

parts.note: sects are religious or political groups

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters, its contents removed

explanation.surface: Someone single is set apart because they feel no love within their social circles.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick or choose, the same as singling out.

clue.text: Old lines blokes tell originally about junk's exaggeration

indicators.note: the poetic lines go around the word for junk

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry
tat is cheap junk; the 's is read as is, a link
men, as blokes are

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tell is taken

explanation.surface: Old poems told by men, about rubbish, are dismissed as hyperbole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tat' is British slang for cheap, shoddy goods; 'about' has the lines wrap it, and 'originally' takes only the first letter of tell.
explanation.definitionFit: An overstatement says more than is true, which is what exaggeration means.

clue.text: Rose quickly and staggered clutching edges of table

indicators.note: the word for staggered holds the two letters inside it

parts.note: rocked means swayed or staggered

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A drunk got up fast and wobbled, gripping the sides of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rocketed soared or shot upward fast, like prices.

clue.text: Fertiliser gathered under avian nests, organic initially

indicators.note: the opening letters of the five words that follow are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Organic fertiliser is collected from beneath birds' nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is bird or bat droppings used as a natural manure for crops.

clue.text: Members with Air Miles both gutted

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its insides, leaving only first and last letters

explanation.surface: Frequent-flyer club members have had their air miles cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are limbs, and limbs are often called members.

clue.text: 'Jazz' by Queen, a grand release in comeback

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the word for release is turned backwards, coming back

parts.note: emit means give out or release

explanation.surface: A queen's jazz record and a grand comeback release.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is an early syncopated piano style that led into jazz.

clue.text: Where test involved grasping a flame

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the single letter inside them
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a test involved holding a burning flame.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former lover, so flame means a sweetheart.

clue.text: Reserve holding opener for lotion or ointment

indicators.note: the word for reserve has the letter placed within it

parts.note: to save is to reserve or keep back

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Keep back the first dab of lotion or cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lotion' looks like part of the definition, but only its first letter is used; 'or' joins wordplay to 'ointment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing balm rubbed on the skin, an ointment.

clue.text: Wine in imitation piece of glass, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken and the answer only sounds like them

parts.note: sham means fake or imitation; a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: Wine served in a fake glass, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Divine erotic snap got hacked

indicators.note: hacked means chopped about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy photo was obtained by hacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective praising the snap, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foresee or predict, the same as forecasting the future.

clue.text: Make-up artist's alien accepted by astronomer

indicators.note: the alien is taken into the middle of the scientist's title

parts.note: a cosmologist studies the universe, a kind of astronomer
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A make-up artist is an alien taken in by a stargazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetologist is a beautician skilled in applying cosmetics.

clue.text: Finest travelled by horse and dominated

parts.note: best means finest
ridden describes a horse that has been ridden on

explanation.surface: The best horse ridden, and victorious.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to stand astride and lord it over, hence dominated.

clue.text: Novel and elves — bound to work?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fantasy novel whose elves are forced into labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enslaved is held in bondage and compelled to labour, the question mark marking the playful definition.

clue.text: Violent explosion under the bridge?

parts.note: the bridge is the bony ridge of the nose, and the burst of air beneath it is a nasal outburst

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bomb under a river crossing; the bridge is the nose's.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden convulsive expulsion of air through the nose is exactly this reflex.

clue.text: Run down wildcat beneath lair

indicators.note: in a down entry the wildcat comes below, so after the lair

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A wildcat is hunted down below its den.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to criticise them publicly, to run them down.

clue.text: Scathing about for instance flipping butt

indicators.note: the word for scathing goes around the turned abbreviation

parts.note: a tart remark is sharp or scathing

indicators.note: flipping turns the abbreviation over, reading it backwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about someone's flipping backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The butt of a joke is its target, the object of ridicule.

clue.text: Artist's music style, heavenly on and off

parts.note: rap is a style of music

indicators.note: letters are taken and skipped in turn, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An artist's music is now and then heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Artist's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was the Italian Renaissance painter of the School of Athens.

clue.text: Possibly sew name right in trousers?

indicators.note: possibly signals an arrangement other than the one shown

explanation.surface: A tailor might stitch a name properly into a pair of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are one example of men's clothing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Apprentice stupidly holding leads on

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A trainee foolishly strings someone along.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt, the same as leading someone on.

clue.text: Painter, I rework Monet's 'Irises', power replacing energy

indicators.note: to rework is to reshape, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for power takes the place of the letter for energy

parts.note: the name with its S included as fodder
E is the physics symbol for energy
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A painter reworks Monet's famous Irises.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping P for E gives MONTSP, and with I and IRISES those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An Impressionist is a member of the movement led by Monet and Renoir.

clue.text: Country, in origin, somewhere around Micronesia or Australia

indicators.note: the origin of each word is its first letter, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A Pacific nation lying somewhere near Micronesia or Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an independent island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Endure time in express

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the word for express

parts.note: to say is to express

explanation.surface: Bear the time spent on an express train.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to last or persist, so it can mean endure.

clue.text: Financial paper's in crisis with new document-writer

indicators.note: the paper's abbreviation sits inside the word for crisis

parts.note: a drama is a crisis or exciting turn of events
FT is the Financial Times newspaper, and the 's supplies S

explanation.surface: A financial newspaper is in crisis and needs a new writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftsman draws up legal documents or technical drawings, so writes them.

clue.text: Ace bed after taking in second course

indicators.note: the two pieces, once they have absorbed the letter, give the answer

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A great bed, after taking a second course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is not a meal course but a racecourse: Ascot is the English racecourse famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England, home of the royal race meeting.

clue.text: River duck going to east

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, nil
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A duck on a river heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batter's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river flowing through Egypt.

clue.text: Fondle embracing the French lovely ends with haste

indicators.note: the word for fondle holds the French article inside it

parts.note: to caress is to fondle
le is French for the

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hurried fondle and embrace ends something lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carelessly means doing it hastily and without proper attention.
